notes: Best verification of the iteration: four independent verifier subagents, each given 2-4 neutrally worded candidates without the reviewer's reasoning, covered all 12 Medium+ candidates and refuted none; one verifier added a caveat (main has no duplicate guard either) that the report records. Only run where verification fully matched the skill's design. Misses S4 entirely. S9: every run names the call-site '-' strip as a bypass of parse_money's non-negative guard, but none says the fix 'belongs in util.parse_money'. All instead cite the parse_money docstring ('adjustments are modeled explicitly') and propose an explicit credit model. I graded S9 on the named mechanism (call-site special case working around the helper) and passed it uniformly. The assertion's remedy clause conflicts with the fixture's own docstring and should be reworded, e.g. 'flags the call-site negative special case as a band-aid around util.parse_money's contract'. S4: no run in the iteration rated the check-then-act race as a PLAUSIBLE Issue as the README expects. Runs that mention it put it in Known limitations or a Fix clause, so a pass means the mechanism is named, not that it is calibrated. S5 passes at Low or Suggestion severity; the assertion does not demand a severity. The skim test is subjective: graded on finding headlines plus the first What sentence, since every headline states the defect and the section gives the severity.
